research_period: Shows 10 September to 6 October 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis October to November 2026
markets: Global: New York, London, Milan, Paris and Copenhagen runways; applies to premium and mid-market womenswear
title: SS27 Women's One-Layer Summer
summary: A summer dressed for heat: sheer suits, featherweight organza tailoring, single-layer knits and perforated leather. Lightness replaces layering as the sign of luxury.

sections.heading: The story
sections.body:
Europe's extreme summer heat shaped the SS27 collections<sup>[1]</sup>. Nicolas Ghesquière put it simply at Louis Vuitton: "We needed to think differently. You want one layer"<sup>[1]</sup>. His collection cut tailoring from the lightest knits and used fabrics as thin as cigarette paper<sup>[2]</sup>. At Dior, Jonathan Anderson made featherweight organza tailoring printed to look like wool suiting, with pleated plissé and petals<sup>[1]</sup>, and sheer suits with mesh blazers<sup>[2]</sup>. Hermès perforated suede for airflow<sup>[1]</sup> and showed sheer knits<sup>[2]</sup>. In Milan, Armani, Missoni, Max Mara and Ferragamo showed see-through dresses and veiled skirts and trousers<sup>[2]</sup>.

The result is a new idea of summer polish: a complete, tailored look that weighs almost nothing.

sections.heading: Colours
sections.body: Optic white, butter and lilac from the SS27 womenswear palette, with pale tones that show the transparency of the cloth. See SS27 Women's Season Colour Analysis for codes.

sections.heading: Silhouettes
sections.body:
- Sheer suits: unlined jackets and straight or full skirts in organza or mesh.
- Single-layer knit tailoring: a fine knit jacket worn alone.
- Layered midi skirts in two or three sheer layers.
- Sheer fine-gauge tops over slips or bandeaus.

sections.heading: Fabrics
sections.body: Organza, chiffon, tulle and mesh<sup>[2]</sup>; nylon organza, double gauze and devoré chiffon<sup>[3]</sup>; fine wool and extra-fine merino<sup>[4]</sup>; perforated leather and suede<sup>[1]</sup>.

sections.heading: Trims and details
sections.body: Narrow rolled hems, French seams, ribbon binding, organza petals, minimal hardware.

timing: In stores February to July 2027, strongest for the high-summer drop. Forecut expects single-layer tailoring to remain relevant as summers get hotter.
products:
- Sheer organza jacket and skirt sets; mesh blazers; fine knit jackets.
- Sheer layered midi skirts; sheer blouses with matching slips.
- Customers: city customers in hot climates who still dress for work and occasions; resort and holiday buyers.
design_implications:
- Design every sheer piece with its under-layer.
- Keep construction invisible: French seams, rolled hems, no heavy facings.
- Print or weave tailoring codes (pinstripes, checks) onto light cloth to keep a suit reading as a suit.
commercial_implications:
- Sell sheer suits as sets with under-layers to raise the average order.
- Market to hot-climate regions (Gulf, India, Southeast Asia, Australia) with modest styling options.
- Watch return rates; show what is worn underneath on product pages.
